subject: Materials Science
title: Fatigue: Death by a Thousand Cycles
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fatigue: Death by a Thousand Cycles.

hook.text: An aircraft wing flexes up and down every flight. After millions of cycles, a tiny crack appears — and grows.

buildup.text: Fatigue failure occurs below yield strength — repeated loading nucleates and grows cracks over time.

discovery.text: An S-N curve plots stress against cycles to failure — below the endurance limit, steel lasts forever.

twist.text: Aluminum has no endurance limit — given enough cycles, any stress level will eventually cause failure.

climax.text: The 1954 de Havilland Comet crashes were caused by fatigue cracks at square window corners — changing aviation forever.

punchline.text: A stress too small to notice once can kill after a million repetitions.

quiz.question: What is unique about fatigue failure?
options: It only happens above yield strength
It occurs below yield strength after many repeated load cycles
